modes.title: Three ways to play
modes.subtitle: Taboo-style Forbidden Words, forehead Heads Up, or find the Imposter. One phone, three kinds of chaos.
modes.tabooBody: Describe the main word, take bigger risks, and grow your score. Harder words unlock higher multipliers, from ×2 to ×5.
modes.headsUpBody: Phone on your forehead. Friends give clues. Tilt down when you guess right.

showcase.buildScoreBody: Take on harder words to grow your multiplier and turn every correct answer into a bigger score.

modes.imposterBody: One of you doesn't know the word. Everyone else sees it, says one clue word each, and votes to find the imposter before they blend in.

howToPlay.title: How to play every mode
howToPlay.subtitle: The same rules you see in the app. Learn each mode, then start in seconds.

difficulty.title: Every word has a difficulty
difficulty.subtitle: Harder words score more. That keeps rounds competitive and fair for every group.
difficulty.scoreBody: When your team gets it right, tap Correct and take the points. Harder words have a higher multiplier.
difficulty.tabooPenalty: Say a forbidden word? You lose the card. No points for that round.

steps.title: Describe the word
steps.body: Tell your team the word at the top. Never say the 4 forbidden words underneath. Guess as many cards as you can before time runs out.

steps.title: Taboo!
steps.body: Say a forbidden word and you lose the card. No points. The other team keeps the momentum.

steps.title: Pass
steps.body: Stuck? Pass the card. You only get a few passes per turn, so save them for the hard ones.

steps.title: Correct scores more
steps.body: When your team gets it, hit Correct and take the points. Harder words have a higher multiplier.

steps.title: Phone on your forehead
steps.body: Hold the phone in landscape and place it on your forehead. Friends see the word. You do not.

steps.title: They clue, you guess
steps.body: The player with the phone on their forehead cannot see the word. Everyone else reads it on screen and gives verbal clues. There is no pass button.

steps.title: Got it
steps.body: Got it? Nod your chin down, tilt the phone down on your forehead. You score a point and the next word appears.

steps.title: Didn't know
steps.body: Don't know it? Nod your chin up, tilt the phone up on your forehead. No point. Move to the next word.

steps.title: Write any topic
steps.body: Type a word, a phrase, or a full sentence. Coffee, 90s hits, Oscar films. One idea is enough.

steps.title: Add more ideas
steps.body: Tap + to stack topics, or pick a suggestion. Tap a chip to remove it.

steps.title: Language and difficulty
steps.body: Deck language is the card language. Difficulty sets how hard the forbidden words get.

steps.title: Play it in both modes
steps.body: The same deck works in Forbidden Words and Heads Up. Pick the mode when you tap the deck.

steps.title: Generate in seconds
steps.body: Sign in, then tap Create. Your custom deck is ready to play right away.

faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before your next game night.

items.q: How do you play Taboo (Forbidden Words)?
items.a: Split into teams. One player describes the target word without saying any forbidden clues on the card. Your team guesses before time runs out. Passes are limited. Tadado includes timers, scoring, and themed decks so you can start in seconds.

items.q: How do you play Heads Up charades?
items.a: Hold the phone on your forehead so you cannot see the word. Friends give clues without saying the word. Tilt down when you guess correctly, tilt up to skip. Tadado uses the same decks in Heads Up and Taboo modes.

items.q: How do you play Imposter in Tadado?
items.a: Pass one phone around. Everyone sees the same secret word except the imposter, whose card is blank. Take turns saying one clue word, then vote on who the imposter is. If caught, the imposter can still win by guessing the word.

items.q: What is a good Halloween party game for a group?
items.a: Tadado works well for Halloween parties: the free Halloween deck has 100 spooky words like Werewolf, Witch and Haunted house, and you can play it as Taboo-style Forbidden Words, Heads Up or Imposter on one phone. No cards, no setup, no ads.

items.q: Is Tadado one of the best free party game apps?
items.a: Tadado is built for game night: Taboo-style Forbidden Words, Heads Up charades, the Imposter bluffing game, free decks, optional themed decks and AI deck creation. No ads and no subscription, which makes it one of the best value party game apps on iOS and Android.
Yes. Tadado Mix is free to play. Optional theme decks and AI deck creation are one-time purchases. See Pricing for details. There is no subscription.

items.q: What is the difference between Taboo and Heads Up?
items.a: Forbidden Words is team-based Taboo: describe without forbidden words. Heads Up puts the phone on your forehead while friends give clues. Both use the same decks.
No. Tadado is ad-free. You only pay for optional decks or AI creation if you choose.

items.q: How does AI deck creation work?
items.a: Write a topic, like "Marvel movies" or "90s pop hits", and Tadado generates a playable deck in seconds for Forbidden Words and Heads Up.
The app UI is available in 17 languages including English, Turkish, Spanish, German, French, and more.

halloweenPage.metaDescription: The easiest Halloween party games for friends and family: spooky Taboo, Heads Up and Imposter on one phone with a free 100-word Halloween deck. No cards, no ads.
halloweenPage.h1: Halloween Party Games on One Phone
halloweenPage.answer: The easiest Halloween party game for a group is one that needs no cards and no setup. Tadado turns one phone into three Halloween games: spooky Taboo (Forbidden Words), Heads Up and Imposter, all with a free deck of 100 Halloween words. It works for 3 to 20+ players, friends, families and office parties.

faq.q: What is the best Halloween game for a group of friends?
faq.a: A game that needs no prep and gets everyone talking. Tadado's free Halloween deck lets a group play spooky Taboo, Heads Up or Imposter on one phone, so the game starts as soon as people arrive.

faq.q: Is the Tadado Halloween deck free?
faq.a: Yes. The Halloween deck is free for every player, with 100 Halloween words. There are no ads and no subscription.
From 3 players up to big parties. Taboo and Heads Up split the room into teams, and Imposter takes 3 to 12 players on one phone.

faq.q: Is it good for kids and family Halloween parties?
faq.a: Yes. The deck is built around Halloween classics like Pumpkin, Witch, Ghost and Trick or treat, so it suits family nights as well as adult parties.

faq.q: Do we need cards or extra phones?

faq.q: Which languages does the Halloween deck support?
